name: Quality Control Checklist
description: A quality control (QC) checklist for inspecting product and output against specifications.

items.text: Obtain the current product specification and drawings.
Confirm acceptance criteria and tolerances.
items.note: Use the specification and standards that apply to your product.

items.text: Define the sampling plan and inspection level.
Verify measurement equipment is calibrated and in date.
Prepare reference samples, gauges and check fixtures.
Confirm the inspection method and recording format.
Verify received goods match the purchase order and packing list.
Check supplier certificates and material documentation.
Inspect quantity, lot numbers and packaging condition.
Sample and measure key characteristics against specification.
Quarantine material until inspection is complete.
Accept, reject or hold the lot and record the decision.
Confirm the first-off sample meets specification before the run continues.
Inspect at set intervals during production.
Measure critical dimensions and characteristics.
Check appearance, fit and function as required.
Monitor process trends for drift toward limits.
Segregate any nonconforming product immediately.
Inspect finished product against the full specification.
Verify dimensions, function and performance.
Check labeling, markings and packaging.
Confirm required documentation accompanies the product.
Apply the sampling plan and record results.
Release, hold or reject the lot and document the decision.
Identify and classify defects by type and severity.
Compare defect counts against acceptance limits.
Label and isolate nonconforming product.
Decide disposition: rework, scrap, concession or return.
Raise a nonconformance report where required.
Notify suppliers or upstream processes of recurring defects.
Record measurements, sample sizes and results.
Document accept and reject decisions with inspector sign-off.
Maintain traceability to lot, batch or serial numbers.
Summarize defect rates and inspection findings.
Share quality data with production and suppliers.
File records for traceability and audit.

faq.a: Quality control is the inspection side of quality — checking product or output against specifications at incoming, in-process and final stages, sampling for defects and recording results so only conforming product is released.

faq.q: What is the difference between QC and QA?
faq.a: Quality control (QC) inspects the product to catch defects. Quality assurance (QA) builds quality into the process through procedures, standards and training so fewer defects occur. QC detects, QA prevents.

Acceptance sampling means inspecting a representative sample from a lot, rather than every unit, and using defined limits to accept or reject the whole lot. Sampling plans balance inspection cost against the risk of passing defects.

faq.q: How do I handle defective product?
faq.a: Identify, segregate and clearly label nonconforming product so it cannot move forward. Record the defect, decide on disposition such as rework, scrap or concession, and follow your organization's procedures and standards.

faq.q: Is this available as a printable PDF?
faq.a: Yes. Print the quality control checklist for the inspection station, or download the PDF so inspectors can record measurements, defects and accept or reject decisions and keep records on file.
